title: Power chords B B A A G G F# F# B B A A G G E E 140bpm Les Paul
timingNotes: Onsets are pick-attack transients on a three-pole 5kHz-highpassed 1ms RMS envelope, backtracked to 30% of each attack peak above its local floor; the sixteen attacks stand 10-30x above every other peak in that band, so the count is unambiguous. Measured inter-onset intervals are 815-885ms (mean 857.2ms). STRUCTURE: the take is at 140bpm like the rest of the session, and the performer struck only on alternate beats -- 857ms is a HALF note at that tempo, not a slower quarter. In his words, he played only on note boundaries. The figure is chord X, X again and then muted, chord Y, Y again and then muted: B B A A | G G F# F# | B B A A | G G E E. That is exactly the figure the performer described, event for event; an earlier version of this note read 857ms as a half note at 140bpm and concluded the audio contradicted him, which was wrong. There is no quieter re-strum between these sixteen, and the weaker transients that sit between them are the muting hand rather than a pick. That was settled on the DI capture of this same performance (fixtures/labels/power-chords-di-...), whose noise floor is 24x lower than this room mic's: every flux peak there that is not one of the sixteen is followed by a FALL in 30ms RMS of 2-22dB where each of the sixteen is followed by a rise of 12-55dB, and a targeted scan of the quarter-note midpoint after each strum (+428.6ms +-120ms) finds a maximum 60ms RMS rise of 1.6-5.0dB against 18-60dB at the strums themselves. The DI aligns to this file at a constant offset of 6052ms and a time-scale of exactly 1.000x, and all sixteen events correspond one to one. The 140bpm clock of the session is confirmed by the cowboy-chord takes, whose bars measure 1714ms; this take places one strum every half note rather than every quarter. Identity comes from FFT peak picking on 8192- and 32768-point windows 100-300ms into each note. Every chord is root+fifth+octave on the low E and A strings; strong partials two octaves and a major third above each root (A#4 over F#2, G#4 over E2, C#5 over A2, B4 over G2, D#5 over B2) are the fifth harmonic of the root, not a major third in the voicing. End times are where each note's RMS falls below 15% of its attack peak: the second note of each pair is muted about 360ms in, leaving a real gap before the next pair. No detector output was used to derive any value here.
